builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
summary: It replaces ad hoc live-site or text-only web-agent evaluation with 300 reproducible tasks across 20 self-hosted applications spanning text, vision, audio, and video. The cost is infrastructure and operational effort to self-host the applications and run isolated parallel evaluations, plus dependence on API access for the strongest agents; it measures agent quality rather than improving it. It can fail to transfer if the reader's production tasks differ from the benchmark's application categories, if self-hosting drifts from the released configurations, or if API model updates change agent behavior between evaluations.
rationale: A reproducible multimodal benchmark is directly useful for validating web agents before production adoption, but the reader should first confirm that its task domains and self-hosting requirements match their workload and budget.

claims.statement: It replaces ad hoc live-site or text-only web-agent evaluation with 300 reproducible tasks across 20 self-hosted applications spanning text, vision, audio, and video. The cost is infrastructure and operational effort to self-host the applications and run isolated parallel evaluations, plus dependence on API access for the strongest agents; it measures agent quality rather than improving it. It can fail to transfer if the reader's production tasks differ from the benchmark's application categories, if self-hosting drifts from the released configurations, or if API model updates change agent behavior between evaluations.

Best agents (Codex with GPT 6.1 Sol, Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5) reach 62.3% task success; strongest generic configurations reach 30.3%, so results are reported as absolute accuracy, not as a multiplicative improvement over a prior method.
